title: Suppliers get payment terms (days), shown in every supplier listing
notes: Reference change: new column supplier.payment_terms_days (INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30) in schema.sql; Supplier record gets int paymentTermsDays with DEFAULT_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS = 30 and a backward-compatible 5-argument constructor; DataStore threads the column through createSupplier, updateSupplier and every query that builds a Supplier: the look-alike listings listSuppliersByName, listSuppliersByCountry, listSuppliersByMinimumRating and findSupplierById (four near-identical SELECT id, name, contact_email, country, rating FROM supplier queries), plus the reports that embed a Supplier: listPurchaseSuggestionsByWarehouse, findPurchasedQuantityPerSupplier, listSupplierPerformance, findSpendingPerSupplier, findCategoriesWithSingleSupplier (the test checks only the listings, the lookup and update). Patch: 3 files, +41/-29. The test reaches the new constructor and accessor by reflection so that it compiles on the untouched code. Verification (scratch copy of variant a, work/tasks-3/verify-<id>): with the acceptance test added to the untouched code the test command compiles and FAILS (2 tests, 2 failures: AssertionFailedError 'A supplier cannot be given payment terms'); after applying reference/a.patch it PASSES and the full `mvn -q -o test` is green. ambiguity_measure.py on the untouched code, methods hit per term: supplier 59, payment terms 0, country 94, rating 13 (median 36.0).
